scope: Observed sessions and GitHub Actions verification; not human statistics, all-site PASS, billing, or historic model-context isolation

sessions.stopReason: visitor_finished: As a visually critical first-time viewer I followed the gemstone entrance, three-page tutorial, gathered five Garden memories, entered the White City and brought a tile into Diary. The pastel CGI-like fantasy palette and multiplying arches/florals look familiar, with several very faint small labels, but the dated fragment cards and physical polaroid souvenir gave specificity. I have seen a complete keepsake loop and am not pulled into another room now. I stop voluntarily; deeper maps, audio, animations remain unassessed.

visitor_finished: As a simulated ordinary first-time visitor I understood the gem entrance and the basic 0/5 scavenger count. I tapped teddy and cup, saw two different memories, then tapped a flower and got an atmospheric sentence but no count increase. It looked pretty and interactive, but the repeated fragment-card format and unclear reason to collect all five did not pull me onward today. I left at 2/5 naturally, without testing the door, Diary or deeper maps. Not a claim that the artwork or whole site is broken.

visitor_finished: Simulated AI-skeptical first-time viewer. After the glossy pastel entrance, three tutorial images, and the Garden invitation, I still saw repeated luminous fantasy props, abundant florals and arches, and no immediately novel reason for me to engage. I voluntarily left without pressing 'この空へ入る'. This is a bias-sensitive gut reaction, not evidence that the later content, text, or overall artwork is bad. I did not test the garden collectibles, Diary or other maps.

visitor_finished: Simulated dreamcore and liminal-art admirer. The opening portal and tutorials felt very pretty and familiar rather than uncertain or uncanny. On the Garden entrance I tapped the small '夢の見覚え' label and unexpectedly entered a vertically ascending garden; this hidden detour and the solitary petal felt specific, quiet and appealing. I carried the petal into Diary and now stop satisfied after one surprising loop. The regular five-item Garden path, Hotel, Perfume and rest were not tested; this is an artistic reading, not an objective metric.

visitor_finished: Simulated literary reader. I entered Garden, read the hidden note about an erased time, then three fragments: an hourglass flowing backwards, scent lingering in a room no one returns to, and a key that opens memory. Each sentence is understandable; their larger causal relationship is intentionally unexplained. The motifs cohere, although repeated dream/memory/absence and the repeated little-card presentation may become monotonous if many are read at once. I have sampled the prose I came to read and leave at 3/5; I have not tested the ending, Diary or any deeper text, nor proved human readers' comprehension.
